Spanish moss is not a type of moss [d1][d2][d3][d5]. According to multiple sources, it belongs to the family Bromeliaceae (the bromeliads), making it more closely related to pineapples than to true mosses [d1][d3][d5]. As d3 explains, "Spanish moss isn't really a type of moss. (Mosses grow from spores, not seeds.) Spanish moss is a type of bromeliad" [d3]. It is an epiphyte — a plant that clings to trees and absorbs nutrients and water from the air and rain — but it is neither a parasite nor a true moss [d1][d2][d3]. The name "Spanish moss" is considered misleading, likely earned because of its moss-like appearance and its abundance throughout former Spanish colonies of the New World [d5].
